renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: aligner_agreement
  title: Cells called against cells kept by CellBender
  description: |-
    Each point is one aligner route: the cells it called on the horizontal axis and the cells CellBender kept on that route on the vertical axis. It answers whether the routes agree on how many cells the library holds.
    How to read: points on the diagonal mean CellBender kept about as many cells as the aligner called. A point far from the diagonal, or a route far from the others, means that route calls cells differently, so compare its barcode overlap in the cell-call UpSet before trusting its counts.
    Lines and annotations: the diagonal is y = x, where both counts are equal. It is a reference defined by the data, not a quality cut-off.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/scrnaseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Cells called by the aligner route
    y_title: Cells kept by CellBender
    reference_line: diagonal
    reference_label: equal counts
  roles:
    x: cells_called
    y: cellbender_cells
    label: aligner
    color: aligner

- component: figure
  id: aligner_cells_bar
  title: Cells called per aligner route
  description: |-
    Each bar is an aligner route, as nf-core/scrnaseq runs them with its --aligner option, and its height is the number of cells that route called. It answers which route finds more or fewer cells.
    How to read: similar bar heights mean the routes agree on the library. A route far below the rest may have mapped fewer reads to cells, so check its mapping rate and its barcode overlap with the others.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of cells called of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Cell Ranger.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/scrnaseq/master/nextflow_schema.json
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: aligner
    y: cells_called
    color: aligner
    labels:
      aligner: Aligner route
      cells_called: Cells called
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: cells_called

- component: interactive
  id: aligner_picker
  title: Aligner route
  description: |-
    Picks one aligner route and filters every tile of the tab to it. It answers how a single route behaves on its own.
    How to read: clear the selection to compare all routes again.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: aligner

- component: card
  title: Cells called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of cells called across the shown routes, and the bars rank the routes that called most. It answers how large the called population is and which route drives it.
    How to read: the minimum and maximum give the range between routes. A wide range means the routes disagree on what counts as a cell.
  column: cells_called
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: aligner
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: cells called, by route

- component: card
  title: Mapping rate
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average fraction of reads each route maps to the transcriptome, and the box shows the spread between routes. It answers how well reads land on the reference.
    How to read: a route far below the others lost reads at alignment, so check the reference and the library chemistry. Each tool defines its mapping rate in its own way, so compare routes with care.
    Note: 10x gives an expected value of more than 30 percent for the confidently mapped transcriptome fraction of Cell Ranger only, so no pass mark is drawn here.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf
  column: mapping_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mapping rate, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Aligner routes
  description: |-
    Each row is an aligner route with its cells called, cells kept by CellBender, median UMI per cell and mapping rate. It answers the exact numbers behind the other tiles.
    How to read: sort a column to rank the routes. An empty cell means that route does not report that metric.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: barcode_rank_knee
  title: Barcode rank plot
  description: |-
    Each point is a barcode ranked by its UMI count, from the richest droplet down, on log axes, with one curve per sample. It answers where real cells stop and empty droplets start.
    How to read: a good library has a plateau of cells with high counts, a steep drop, then a long tail of background. A curve with no clear drop means the cells are not well separated from ambient RNA, so check the cell calls and the aligner summary.
    Lines and annotations: the cut-off marks the barcodes the pipeline called as cells. It is the call made by the cell-calling step of the run, not a fixed UMI value.
  kind: knee_plot
  roles:
    sample: sample
    rank: rank
    umi_count: umi_count
    is_cell: is_cell

- component: figure
  id: barcode_rank_curve
  title: Barcode rank curve
  description: |-
    Each point is a barcode: its rank by UMI count on the horizontal axis and its UMI count on the vertical axis, one line per sample. It answers how deep the counts of the best barcodes are and how fast they fall.
    How to read: compare the plateau height and the position of the drop between samples. A lower plateau or an earlier drop means fewer or poorer cells in that library.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: rank
    y: umi_count
    color: sample
    log_x: 'true'
    log_y: 'true'
    labels:
      rank: Barcode rank
      umi_count: UMI count
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: Deepest barcode
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest UMI count of any barcode, and the histogram shows the distribution of the ranked barcodes. It answers how rich the best droplet is.
    How to read: a very high maximum next to a modest median points to a few outlier droplets such as doublets or debris. Open the rank plot to see where they sit.
  column: umi_count
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: UMI counts of ranked barcodes

- component: interactive
  id: barcode_umi_filter
  title: UMI count range
  description: |-
    Restricts the tab to barcodes whose UMI count falls inside the range. It answers which barcodes lie in a chosen depth window.
    How to read: drag the handles to keep only the cell plateau or only the background.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: umi_count

- component: table
  title: Ranked barcodes
  description: |-
    Each row is a barcode with its rank, UMI count and whether the run called it a cell. It answers the exact values behind the curve.
    How to read: sort by rank to see the last barcode called as a cell and the first one rejected.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cell_call_upset
  title: Cells shared between aligner routes
  description: |-
    Each column is a group of barcodes called a cell by exactly the routes whose dots are filled, and its bar is the number of barcodes. It answers which routes agree on each cell and which call cells alone.
    How to read: a tall bar on the full set means all routes agree, and the more barcodes sit there, the more robust the cell calls. Tall bars on single routes mean that route calls many cells the others do not, so inspect its cell QC.
    Lines and annotations: bars are coloured by how many routes share the barcodes (the degree of the intersection). No cut-off is drawn.
  kind: upset_plot
  config:
    color_intersections_by: degree

- component: interactive
  id: caller_count_filter
  title: Number of routes agreeing
  description: |-
    Keeps the barcodes that at least the chosen number of routes call as cells. It answers how the picture changes when only well-supported cells are kept.
    How to read: raise the lower handle to see the consensus cells only.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: n_callers

- component: card
  title: Routes agreeing on a barcode
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of routes that call a barcode a cell, and the box shows the spread. It answers how much the routes agree overall.
    How to read: a median near the number of routes means strong agreement. A low median means most cells are called by one route only.
  column: n_callers
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: routes per barcode, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Barcodes called as cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of barcodes called a cell by at least one route, and the strip shows how many of them are unique. It answers how large the union of cell calls is.
    How to read: a count much larger than a single route's cell count means the routes call different barcodes.
  column: barcode_core
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: uniqueness
  caption: barcodes called by any route

- component: table
  title: Cell calls per barcode
  description: |-
    Each row is a barcode with a true or false for every route that called it a cell and the number of routes that did. It answers which routes called a given barcode.
    How to read: filter on the number of routes to list the contested barcodes.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: phase_scatter
  title: S and G2/M scores per cell
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell: its S-phase score on the horizontal axis and its G2/M score on the vertical axis, coloured by the phase assigned. It answers which cells are cycling and in which phase.
    How to read: a large cloud in the lower left corner is G1 or resting cells, the normal majority of a tissue sample. Arms toward the upper or right regions are cycling cells, so check whether a cluster is mostly cycling before treating it as a distinct cell type.
    Lines and annotations: the two lines sit at a score of 0 on each axis. A cell with both scores negative is called G1, otherwise the higher score gives S or G2M, the rule of scanpy's score_genes_cell_cycle. The gene sets are the S and G2/M sets of Tirosh et al.; the scores here subtract the cell's mean expression instead of expression-matched control genes.
    Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scverse/scanpy/main/src/scanpy/tools/_score_genes.py and https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/cell_cycle_vignette
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: S-phase score
    y_title: G2/M-phase score
    quadrants:
      x: 0
      y: 0
      labels:
      - G2M
      - S or G2M
      - G1
      - S
  roles:
    x: s_score
    y: g2m_score
    color: phase
    label: barcode

- component: figure
  id: phase_by_cluster
  title: Cell-cycle phase per cluster
  description: |-
    Each bar is a cluster and its segments count the cells in each cell-cycle phase. It answers which clusters are made of cycling cells.
    How to read: a cluster dominated by S and G2M cells is a proliferating population, and its markers may reflect the cycle rather than a cell type. A cluster of mostly G1 cells is resting.
    Source: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    color: phase
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      phase: Phase

- component: interactive
  id: phase_filter
  title: Cell-cycle phase
  description: |-
    Keeps only the cells in the chosen phases. It answers how the tab looks for cycling or resting cells alone.
    How to read: select S and G2M to isolate proliferating cells.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: phase

- component: card
  title: Cells per phase
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of cells scored and the ring splits them by phase. It answers what share of the cells is cycling.
    How to read: a G1 majority is the usual pattern. A large S or G2M share suggests a proliferating tissue or a culture, and a cell-cycle effect worth regressing out.
  column: barcode
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: phase
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: cells, by phase

- component: card
  title: S-phase score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median S-phase score over the cells, and the box shows its spread. It answers how strongly S-phase genes are expressed overall.
    How to read: the score is relative to the cell's mean expression, so a median near or below zero means most cells do not express S genes above background.
    Source: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle.html
  column: s_score
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: S-phase score, with its spread

- component: card
  title: G2/M-phase score
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median G2/M score over the cells, and the box shows its spread. It answers how strongly G2/M genes are expressed overall.
    How to read: a median near or below zero means most cells are not in G2 or mitosis. A long upper tail holds the dividing cells.
    Source: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.tl.score_genes_cell_cycle.html
  column: g2m_score
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: G2/M score, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Cell-cycle scores per cell
  description: |-
    Each row is a cell with its cluster, S and G2/M scores, assigned phase and the number of genes of each set found in the reference. It answers the exact values behind the tiles.
    How to read: a low gene count in a set means the reference lacks part of the gene set, so its score is less reliable.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: gene_umap
  title: Cells on the UMAP
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell placed by UMAP and coloured by its graph-based cluster. It answers how the cells group by expression and lets a marker gene be painted on the map.
    How to read: separate islands are distinct cell populations, and touching islands are related states. Pick a gene to colour by to see which cluster expresses it, and select cells to compare them in the group comparison tile.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: UMAP
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: umap_1
    dim_2: umap_2
    cluster: cluster_label
    color: cluster_label

- component: advanced_viz
  id: selection_compare
  title: Compare two groups of cells
  description: |-
    Each row of the result is a gene tested between two chosen cell groups, with its fold change and adjusted p-value. It answers which genes separate one cluster from another.
    How to read: pick two groups and run the test. Genes with a large fold change and a small adjusted p-value mark the difference, and a group with few cells gives little power, so read small groups with care.
    Lines and annotations: the fold-change and false discovery rate cut-offs drawn are the defaults of this tile, not values read from Cell Ranger.
  kind: group_compare
  roles:
    index: barcode
    group: cluster_label

- component: interactive
  id: cell_cluster_picker
  title: Cluster
  description: |-
    Keeps only the cells of the chosen clusters. It answers how a few clusters look on their own.
    How to read: clear the selection to show every cluster again.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: cluster_label

- component: interactive
  id: cell_qc_status_picker
  title: Cell QC status
  description: |-
    Keeps the cells that pass the quality filter or the ones it flagged. It answers whether flagged cells cluster together.
    How to read: show flagged cells to see whether they form a cluster of their own.
  interactive_type: SegmentedControl
  column_name: qc_status

- component: card
  title: Cells per cluster
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of cells shown and the ring splits them by cluster. It answers how the cells divide between clusters.
    How to read: a cluster holding most cells dominates the map. A very small cluster may be a rare population or a quality artefact.
  column: barcode
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: cluster_label
  top_n_count: 5
  caption: cells, by cluster

- component: figure
  id: marker_by_cluster
  title: Marker expression per cluster
  description: |-
    Each box is a cluster and shows the expression of the selected marker genes over its cells. It answers which clusters express a marker.
    How to read: a high box in one cluster and low boxes elsewhere marks a cluster-specific gene. Boxes pinned at zero mean the gene is rarely detected there, which is common for lowly expressed genes.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    y: expression
    color: cluster_label
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      expression: Expression (log1p CP10k)

- component: figure
  id: marker_by_gene
  title: Marker expression per gene
  description: |-
    Each box is a marker gene and shows its expression over the cells in view. It answers which markers are expressed strongly and how widely.
    How to read: a wide box with a high median is a robust marker. A box squeezed at zero with a few high points is detected in only a small fraction of cells.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: gene
    y: expression
    color: gene
    labels:
      gene: Gene
      expression: Expression (log1p CP10k)

- component: interactive
  id: marker_gene_picker
  title: Marker gene
  description: |-
    Shows one marker gene on every tile of the tab. It answers how a single gene behaves.
    How to read: clear the selection to show all markers again.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: gene

- component: interactive
  id: marker_expression_filter
  title: Expression range
  description: |-
    Keeps the cells whose expression falls inside the range. It answers which cells express a gene above a level.
    How to read: raise the lower handle above zero to keep only the cells where the gene is detected.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: expression

- component: card
  title: Marker expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median expression of the marker genes over the cells in view, and the box shows its spread. It answers how strongly the markers are expressed.
    How to read: a median at zero is normal for sparse single-cell data, so read the upper whisker and the maximum for signal.
  column: expression
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: expression, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Marker expression per cell
  description: |-
    Each row is one gene in one cell with its cluster, QC status and expression. It answers the exact values behind the box plots.
    How to read: filter on a gene and sort by expression to find the cells that express it most.

- component: card
  id: cell_waterfall
  title: From barcodes to cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of barcodes observed, and the waterfall steps down to the cells called, the cells CellBender kept and the cells that pass the quality filter. It answers how many droplets end up as usable cells.
    How to read: a large first step is normal, since most barcodes are empty droplets. A big loss at a later step means cell calling or the quality filter removed many cells.
  column: barcodes_observed
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: attrition
  attrition_cols:
  - cells_called
  - cellbender_cells
  - cells_qc_pass
  caption: barcodes down to cells passing QC

- component: card
  title: Barcodes observed
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of barcodes seen across samples, and the box shows how that varies per sample. It answers how deeply each library was sampled.
    How to read: a sample far from the others was loaded or sequenced differently, so check its sequencing depth before comparing it.
  column: barcodes_observed
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  - count
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: barcodes per sample, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Cells called
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of cells called across samples, and the histogram shows the distribution per sample. It answers how many cells each library yields.
    How to read: a sample with few cells has less power in every downstream tile.
  column: cells_called
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: cells called per sample

- component: card
  title: Cells passing QC
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of called cells that pass the quality filter, and the gauge shows it out of 100 percent. It answers how clean the called cells are.
    How to read: the minimum shows the worst sample. A low value points to many cells with few genes, few UMIs or a high mitochondrial share.
    Note: the filter uses median absolute deviation limits computed per sample, see the description of the cell QC tab for the rules.
  column: pct_qc_pass
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: cells passing QC, of 100%

- component: card
  title: Share of barcodes called as cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of observed barcodes called a cell, and the box shows its spread across samples. It answers how selective cell calling is.
    How to read: the value depends on loading and ambient RNA, so compare samples of one experiment, not absolute levels. An outlier sample deserves a look at its barcode rank plot.
  column: pct_called
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: share of barcodes called, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Cell counts per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its barcodes, cells called, cells kept by CellBender, cells passing QC and the two shares. It answers the exact counts behind the cards.
    How to read: follow a row left to right to see where a sample loses cells.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: umap_qc
  title: UMAP coloured by genes detected
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell on the UMAP, coloured by the log10 of the genes it detects. It answers whether depth or quality follows the cell groups.
    How to read: a smooth colour within each island is expected. A whole island of low values is a cluster of poor cells or a low-RNA cell type, so check the mitochondrial and UMI tiles before trusting it.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: UMAP
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: umap_1
    dim_2: umap_2
    color: log10_n_genes
    cluster: graphclust

- component: advanced_viz
  id: umap_label
  title: UMAP coloured by cluster
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell on the UMAP, coloured by its graph-based cluster and named by its top two marker genes. It answers how the cells group by expression.
    How to read: compact, separated islands are distinct populations. A cluster split across the map, or mixed with another, is weakly defined, so compare it with the k-means resolutions in the stability tile.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: UMAP
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: umap_1
    dim_2: umap_2
    cluster: cluster_label
    color: cluster_label

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tsne_label
  title: t-SNE coloured by cluster
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell on the t-SNE map, coloured by its graph-based cluster. It answers whether the grouping seen on the UMAP also holds on a second embedding.
    How to read: clusters that stay compact on both maps are robust. Distances between islands are not meaningful on a t-SNE, so judge membership, not proximity.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: t-SNE
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: tsne_1
    dim_2: tsne_2
    cluster: cluster_label
    color: cluster_label

- component: advanced_viz
  id: umi_vs_genes
  title: Genes detected against UMI counts
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell: its total UMI count on the horizontal axis and the number of genes it detects on the vertical axis, coloured by its QC status. It answers whether cells follow the expected relation between depth and complexity.
    How to read: genes detected rise with UMIs and flatten at high depth. Cells that sit far below the cloud have many UMIs from few genes, which points to low-complexity cells or doublets, and flagged cells should lie at the edges.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. The QC flags come from limits of 5 median absolute deviations on log counts and genes, set per sample.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    log_x: true
    x_title: UMI counts per cell
    y_title: Genes detected per cell
  roles:
    x: n_umi
    y: n_genes
    color: qc_status

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cluster_stability
  title: Cluster stability across resolutions
  description: |-
    Each band is a group of cells that moves from a graph-based cluster to a k-means cluster with 6 groups and then one with 10, sized by cell count. It answers how stable the clusters are when the method and the resolution change.
    How to read: a cluster that flows into one group at every step is stable. A cluster that splits evenly across several groups is weakly defined, so treat its identity with care.
  kind: sankey
  config:
    color_mode: source
  roles:
    steps:
    - graphclust
    - kmeans_6
    - kmeans_10

- component: figure
  id: umi_histogram
  title: UMI counts per cell
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the cells with a total UMI count in a range, split by QC status. It answers how deep the cells are and where the low-depth tail lies.
    How to read: a single peak with a short left tail is a healthy library. A second peak at low counts is empty droplets or debris that the filter flagged.
    The QC filter flags cells below 5 median absolute deviations under the median of log counts, computed per sample.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median UMI count per cell of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the QC filter.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: n_umi
    color: qc_status
    labels:
      n_umi: UMI counts per cell
      qc_status: QC status
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: n_umi

- component: figure
  id: genes_histogram
  title: Genes detected per cell
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the cells with a number of detected genes in a range, split by QC status. It answers how complex the cells are.
    How to read: one peak is a healthy library, and a tail of few genes marks poor cells. Complexity depends on the cell type, so compare it across clusters before filtering.
    The QC filter flags cells below 5 median absolute deviations under the median of log genes, computed per sample.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of genes detected per cell of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the QC filter.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: n_genes
    color: qc_status
    labels:
      n_genes: Genes detected per cell
      qc_status: QC status
  reference_lines:
  - axis: x
    stat: median
    column: n_genes

- component: figure
  id: mito_box
  title: Mitochondrial fraction by cluster
  description: |-
    Each box is a cluster and shows the percent of UMIs from mitochondrial genes in its cells. It answers which clusters carry stressed or dying cells.
    How to read: a cluster with a high box is a candidate for broken cells, but some cell types are naturally rich in mitochondria. Check its markers before removing it.
    The QC filter flags a cell when it exceeds 3 median absolute deviations and a fixed 8 percent, a limit the source calls not universal.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median mitochondrial fraction of a cell of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the QC filter.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    y: pct_mito
    color: cluster_label
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      pct_mito: Mitochondrial UMIs (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: pct_mito

- component: figure
  id: ribo_box
  title: Ribosomal fraction by cluster
  description: |-
    Each box is a cluster and shows the percent of UMIs from ribosomal genes in its cells. It answers which clusters are dominated by ribosomal transcripts.
    How to read: ribosomal content varies a lot between cell types, such as T cells against myeloid cells. A cluster far above the rest is worth a look at its markers, since it may reflect cell type and not quality.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median ribosomal fraction of a cell of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the QC filter.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    y: pct_ribo
    color: cluster_label
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      pct_ribo: Ribosomal UMIs (%)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: pct_ribo

- component: figure
  id: umi_box
  title: UMI counts by cluster
  description: |-
    Each box is a cluster and shows the log10 of the UMI counts of its cells. It answers whether any cluster is much shallower than the others.
    How to read: a cluster well below the rest is either a low-RNA cell type or poor cells. Compare it with the genes detected and the mitochondrial fraction.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median log10 UMI count per cell of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the QC filter.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    y: log10_n_umi
    color: cluster_label
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      log10_n_umi: UMI counts (log10)
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log10_n_umi

- component: figure
  id: qc_status_by_cluster
  title: QC status per cluster
  description: |-
    Each bar is a cluster and its segments count the cells that pass or that the filter flagged. It answers whether flagged cells concentrate in some clusters.
    How to read: a cluster made mostly of flagged cells is probably an artefact and not a cell type. Open the table to see which rule flagged them.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    color: qc_status
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      qc_status: QC status

- component: interactive
  id: qc_reason_picker
  title: QC reason
  description: |-
    Keeps the cells flagged for the chosen reason, or those that pass. It answers which rule removes which cells.
    How to read: select one reason to see where those cells sit on the maps.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: qc_reason

- component: interactive
  id: cluster_picker
  title: Cluster
  description: |-
    Keeps only the cells of the chosen clusters. It answers how the QC metrics look in one population.
    How to read: clear the selection to show every cluster again.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: cluster_label

- component: interactive
  id: qc_status_picker
  title: QC status
  description: |-
    Switches between the cells that pass the quality filter and the cells it flagged. It answers where the flagged cells lie.
    How to read: choose flagged to inspect them on the maps and in the table.
  interactive_type: SegmentedControl
  column_name: qc_status

- component: interactive
  id: n_umi_filter
  title: UMI counts range
  description: |-
    Keeps the cells whose total UMI count falls in the range. It answers how the tab changes when shallow or very deep cells are left out.
    How to read: drag the lower handle to hide the shallow cells.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: n_umi

- component: interactive
  id: n_genes_filter
  title: Genes detected range
  description: |-
    Keeps the cells whose number of detected genes falls in the range. It answers how the tab changes when low-complexity cells are left out.
    How to read: drag the lower handle to hide cells with few genes.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: n_genes

- component: interactive
  id: top20_share_filter
  title: Top 20 gene share range
  description: |-
    Keeps the cells whose top 20 genes hold a share of UMIs inside the range. It answers which cells are dominated by a few genes.
    How to read: drag the upper handle down to hide cells that few genes dominate.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: pct_top20

- component: card
  title: UMI counts per cell
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median UMI count of a cell, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how deeply the cells are sequenced.
    How to read: a median in the thousands is typical for droplet data. A long left tail or a minimum near zero shows cells the filter should remove.
  column: n_umi
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: UMI counts, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Genes detected per cell
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of genes detected in a cell, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how complex the cells are.
    How to read: low values point to poor cells or low-RNA cell types. Compare with the UMI card, since the two rise together.
  column: n_genes
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: genes detected, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Mitochondrial fraction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of UMIs from mitochondrial genes, shown against the fixed limit of 8 percent. It answers whether the typical cell is stressed.
    How to read: a median under the limit passes. A high maximum is a cell the filter flags, together with the median absolute deviation rule.
    Lines and annotations: the 8 percent limit is the fixed cut-off a cell must also exceed to be flagged, besides 3 median absolute deviations. The source states it is not universal because mitochondrial content differs between cell types and tissues.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  column: pct_mito
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 8.0
  threshold_direction: max
  caption: median against the 8% mitochondrial limit

- component: card
  title: Cells flagged by QC
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of cells the quality filter flags, and the bar splits the cells into passing and flagged. It answers how much of the library the filter removes.
    How to read: the average is the flagged fraction. A small fraction is typical, and a large one means the library or the filter settings need a closer look.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  column: qc_flagged
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - average
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: qc_status
  caption: cells passing and flagged

- component: card
  title: Top 20 gene share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of UMIs held by a cell's 20 most expressed genes, and the box shows its spread. It answers how concentrated the expression is.
    How to read: a high share means a few genes dominate the cell, which is typical of low complexity or damaged cells. Cells above 5 median absolute deviations are flagged.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  column: pct_top20
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: top 20 gene share, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Ribosomal fraction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percent of UMIs from ribosomal genes, and the box shows its spread. It answers how much of the signal is ribosomal.
    How to read: the level depends on the cell types in the sample. No cut-off is drawn because the QC rules use no ribosomal limit.
  column: pct_ribo
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: ribosomal share, with its spread

- component: card
  title: UMI counts, log scale
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median log10 of the UMI counts of a cell, and the box shows its spread. It answers the depth of the cells on the scale the QC rule uses.
    How to read: a narrow box means even depth. A long lower whisker holds the shallow cells.
  column: log10_n_umi
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: UMI counts (log10), with their spread

- component: card
  title: Genes detected, log scale
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median log10 of the genes detected in a cell, and the box shows its spread. It answers the complexity of the cells on the scale the QC rule uses.
    How to read: a narrow box means even complexity. A long lower whisker holds the low-complexity cells.
  column: log10_n_genes
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: genes detected (log10), with their spread

- component: card
  title: CellBender cell calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of cells in view and the bar splits them by whether CellBender also kept them. It answers how much the ambient-RNA correction agrees with the cell calls.
    How to read: a bar that is almost entirely kept means the two calls agree. A sizeable dropped share means many called cells are mostly ambient RNA.
  column: cellbender_cell
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: cellbender_cell
  caption: cells kept and dropped by CellBender

- component: table
  title: Cell quality control
  description: |-
    Each row is a cell with its counts, mitochondrial, ribosomal and haemoglobin shares, embedding coordinates, clusters and QC flags. It answers the exact values behind every tile and lets a row selection filter the others.
    How to read: sort by a metric to find the extreme cells, and read the reason column to see which rule flagged a cell.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: barcode

- component: figure
  id: cluster_sizes
  title: Cells per cluster
  description: |-
    Each bar is a graph-based cluster and its height is the number of cells in it. It answers how the cells divide between clusters.
    How to read: a few large clusters with a tail of small ones is typical. A very small cluster can be a rare population or a quality artefact, so check its QC tile.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cluster_label
    y: n_cells
    color: cluster_label
    labels:
      cluster_label: Cluster
      n_cells: Cells

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cluster_qc_heatmap
  title: Quality profile per cluster
  description: |-
    Each row is a cluster and each column a quality measure: median UMIs, median genes, median mitochondrial share, share of flagged cells and share kept by CellBender. It answers which clusters differ in quality from the rest.
    How to read: colours are standardised per column, so a cluster that is dark in the UMI and gene columns and in the flagged column is a poor one. A cluster that stands out only on one measure usually reflects its cell type.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. Each column is scaled to a z-score over the clusters shown, so colours compare clusters and not absolute values.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    normalize: col_z
  roles:
    index: cluster_label
    value_columns:
    - median_n_umi
    - median_n_genes
    - median_pct_mito
    - pct_flagged
    - pct_cellbender_cell
    row_annotation_cols:
    - sample

- component: figure
  id: cluster_composition
  title: Cluster composition per sample
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and its segments are the share of its cells in each cluster. It answers whether the samples contribute evenly to every cluster.
    How to read: similar stacks mean the samples have the same composition. A cluster present in only one sample may be a batch effect or real biology, so check the sample metadata.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: pct_cells
    color: cluster_label
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      pct_cells: Cells (%)
      cluster_label: Cluster

- component: interactive
  id: cluster_size_filter
  title: Cluster size range
  description: |-
    Keeps the clusters whose cell count falls inside the range. It answers how the tab looks without very small or very large clusters.
    How to read: raise the lower handle to hide the smallest clusters.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: n_cells

- component: card
  title: Cells in clusters
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of cells over all clusters and the bars rank the largest clusters. It answers where most of the cells sit.
    How to read: the median gives the size of a typical cluster, and a maximum far above it shows a dominant one.
  column: n_cells
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cluster_label
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: cells, in the largest clusters

- component: card
  title: UMI counts per cluster
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the clusters' median UMI counts, and the box shows their spread. It answers whether the clusters have similar depth.
    How to read: a cluster far below the rest is shallower, either by cell type or by poor quality. Compare it with the mitochondrial and flagged shares.
  column: median_n_umi
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: cluster UMI medians, with their spread

- component: card
  title: Flagged cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average percent of cells per cluster that the quality filter flags, shown out of 100 percent. It answers how many cells the filter would remove.
    How to read: the maximum is the worst cluster. A cluster with a high share is a candidate artefact, and the rule is the median absolute deviation limit set per sample.
    Source: https://www.sc-best-practices.org/preprocessing-visualization/quality-control/
  column: pct_flagged
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: cells flagged, of 100%

- component: card
  title: Cells kept by CellBender
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average percent of a cluster's cells that CellBender also calls cells, shown out of 100 percent. It answers how well the ambient-RNA correction agrees with the called cells.
    How to read: values near 100 mean agreement. The minimum names the cluster that loses most cells, which may be mostly ambient RNA.
  column: pct_cellbender_cell
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: cells kept by CellBender, of 100%

- component: table
  title: Cluster summary
  description: |-
    Each row is a cluster with its cell count, share of the sample, median counts and genes, median mitochondrial share, flagged share and share kept by CellBender. It answers the exact values behind the tiles.
    How to read: sort by a column to rank the clusters on that measure.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cluster_markers
  title: Top markers per cluster
  description: |-
    Each bar is a gene: its log2 fold change in one cluster against all other cells, for the genes with the largest change. It answers which genes characterise each cluster.
    How to read: long bars to the right are markers of that cluster. Bars are marked when their adjusted p-value passes the display limit, and a strong change without it usually comes from very few cells.
    Lines and annotations: the limit is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the cut-off this module's recipe uses to label marker genes, not read from the run. Cell Ranger defines no cut-off for its marker tests.
  kind: da_barplot
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    top_n: 10
  roles:
    feature_id: gene
    contrast: cluster
    lfc: log2fc
    significance: adjusted_pvalue
    label: gene

- component: advanced_viz
  id: cluster_volcano
  title: Marker volcano per cluster
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene tested in one cluster against all other cells: its log2 fold change on the horizontal axis and its adjusted p-value on the vertical axis. It answers which genes separate a cluster and how confidently.
    How to read: genes in the upper right are strong, confident markers of the cluster, and genes in the upper left are depleted in it. Only the most significant genes per cluster are kept, so the lower part of the plot is truncated.
    Lines and annotations: the horizontal line is an adjusted p-value of 0.05, the cut-off this module's recipe uses to label marker genes, not read from the run. No fold-change line is drawn, because Cell Ranger defines no cut-off for its marker tests.
  kind: volcano
  config:
    significance_threshold: 0.05
    effect_threshold: 0.0
    top_n_labels: 10
    effect_label: Log2 fold change
    significance_label: -log10 adjusted p-value
  roles:
    feature_id: gene
    effect_size: log2fc
    significance: adjusted_pvalue
    category: cluster_label
    label: gene

- component: card
  title: Strongest marker per cluster
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest log2 fold change among the marker genes, and the bars rank the clusters with the strongest marker. It answers which clusters are most clearly defined.
    How to read: a cluster with a high top marker is well separated from the others. A low value means its markers are weak, so its identity is less clear.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cluster
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: strongest marker fold change, by cluster

- component: interactive
  id: diffexp_resolution_picker
  title: Clustering resolution
  description: |-
    Switches between the graph-based clustering and the k-means clusterings Cell Ranger ran. It answers how the markers change with the number of clusters.
    How to read: pick one clustering at a time, since a cluster name belongs to one of them.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: resolution

- component: card
  title: Fold change of up markers
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median log2 fold change of the marker genes that are higher in their cluster, and the box shows its spread. It answers how strong the up-regulated markers are.
    How to read: the card keeps only positive changes, because a median over both directions cancels to about zero. A high median means sharply defined clusters.
  column: log2fc
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: pl.col('log2fc') > 0
  caption: fold change of up-regulated markers, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Expression of markers
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the mean UMI counts of the marker genes in their cluster, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers whether the markers are expressed at a usable level.
    How to read: a pile near zero means markers detected in few counts, which are less reliable for annotating a cluster.
  column: mean_counts
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: mean counts of markers, with their spread

- component: table
  title: Cluster marker genes
  description: |-
    Each row is a marker gene of one cluster with its rank, mean counts, log2 fold change and adjusted p-value. It answers the exact statistics behind the plots and lets a row selection filter the others.
    How to read: sort by rank within a cluster to read its best markers first.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: gene

- component: advanced_viz
  id: umap_clusters
  title: UMAP of the cells
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell placed by UMAP and coloured by its graph-based cluster. It answers how the cells group by expression.
    How to read: separate islands are distinct populations and touching islands are related states. Distances between far islands are not reliable, so judge membership and not distance.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: UMAP
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: umap_1
    dim_2: umap_2
    cluster: cluster
    color: cluster

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tsne_clusters
  title: t-SNE of the cells
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell placed by t-SNE and coloured by its graph-based cluster. It answers whether the grouping seen on the UMAP holds on a second embedding.
    How to read: clusters that stay compact on both maps are robust. Distances between islands are not meaningful on a t-SNE.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: t-SNE
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: tsne_1
    dim_2: tsne_2
    cluster: cluster
    color: cluster

- component: advanced_viz
  id: pca_clusters
  title: PCA of the cells
  description: |-
    Each point is a cell on the first three principal components, coloured by its graph-based cluster. It answers which axes of variation separate the clusters.
    How to read: clusters that separate along a component are driven by the genes loading on it. Overlapping clusters are separated only on later components or not at all.
  kind: embedding
  config:
    axis_prefix: PC
  roles:
    sample_id: barcode
    dim_1: pc_1
    dim_2: pc_2
    dim_3: pc_3
    cluster: cluster
    color: cluster

- component: card
  title: Cells per cluster
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct cells and the ring splits them by cluster. It answers how the cells divide between clusters.
    How to read: one cluster holding most cells dominates the maps. A tiny slice may be a rare population or an artefact.
  column: barcode
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: cluster
  caption: cells, by cluster

- component: table
  title: Cell embedding coordinates
  description: |-
    Each row is a cell with its cluster and its coordinates on the UMAP, t-SNE and first three principal components. It answers the exact positions behind the maps.
    How to read: sort by a coordinate to find the cells at the edge of the map.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: hvg_scatter
  title: Gene dispersion against mean expression
  description: |-
    Each point is a gene: its mean expression over the cells on the horizontal axis and its normalised dispersion on the vertical axis, coloured by whether it was kept for the PCA. It answers which genes vary more than expected for their level of expression.
    How to read: the selected genes should sit high above the cloud, since they carry the variation between cell types. Selected genes at very low expression may add noise, and known markers missing from the selection are worth a look.
    Lines and annotations: no line is drawn. The selection is the set Cell Ranger kept for its PCA, and normalised dispersion scales each gene's dispersion by that of genes with similar mean expression.
    Source: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Mean expression (log1p CP10k)
    y_title: Normalised dispersion
    top_n_labels: 10
  roles:
    x: mean_expression
    y: normalized_dispersion
    color: selection
    label: gene

- component: interactive
  id: hvg_selection_filter
  title: Selection status
  description: |-
    Keeps the genes selected for the PCA or the ones left out. It answers what the selection kept and dropped.
    How to read: choose selected to list the genes that shaped the embedding.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: selection

- component: interactive
  id: hvg_dispersion_filter
  title: Normalised dispersion range
  description: |-
    Keeps the genes whose normalised dispersion falls inside the range. It answers which genes vary most.
    How to read: raise the lower handle to keep only the most variable genes.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: normalized_dispersion

- component: card
  title: Genes by selection
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct genes measured and the bars compare the selected and the other genes. It answers how many genes shaped the embedding.
    How to read: a small selected set against a large rest is the usual design. A very small set means few genes carry the variation.
  column: gene
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: selection
  top_n_count: 2
  caption: genes, by selection status

- component: card
  title: Normalised dispersion
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median normalised dispersion of the genes, and the box shows its spread. It answers how variable the typical gene is.
    How to read: dispersion is scaled so a typical gene sits near zero and variable genes lie far above it. The maximum names the most variable gene.
    Source: https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/api/generated/scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes.html
  column: normalized_dispersion
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  - max
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: normalised dispersion, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Detection rate of genes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of cells in which a gene has at least one UMI, and the histogram shows the distribution over genes. It answers how widely genes are detected.
    How to read: most genes are detected in few cells, which is normal for sparse single-cell data. A selected gene with a very low rate drives variation from a few cells.
  column: detection_rate
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share of cells detecting a gene

- component: table
  title: Gene dispersion table
  description: |-
    Each row is a gene with its normalised dispersion, mean expression, detection rate and whether it was selected. It answers the exact values behind the plot.
    How to read: sort by dispersion to list the most variable genes.

- component: interactive
  id: library_metric_picker
  title: Library metric
  description: |-
    Shows one library quality metric at a time. It answers how every sample does on that metric.
    How to read: clear the selection to list the four metrics again.
  interactive_type: Select
  column_name: metric

- component: interactive
  id: library_status_picker
  title: Metric status
  description: |-
    Keeps the metrics that pass or the ones that fall below their expected value. It answers which samples need attention.
    How to read: choose warn or fail to list only the metrics below their limit.
  interactive_type: SegmentedControl
  column_name: status

- component: card
  title: Library metrics by status
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of metric values checked and the bar splits them into pass, warn and fail. It answers how many checks the libraries meet.
    How to read: a bar that is mostly pass means healthy libraries. Open the table to see which sample and metric fell below its limit.
    Lines and annotations: each status compares a value with the expected value 10x gives for that metric: reads in cells above 70 percent, valid barcodes above 75 percent, Q30 of RNA reads above 65 percent and confidently mapped reads above 30 percent. The split between warn and fail is chosen by this catalogue, since the note states one expected value.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf
  column: metric
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: status
  caption: metrics, by status

- component: card
  title: Reads in cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average fraction of reads that fall in called cells, shown against the expected minimum. It answers whether the library is rich in cells and poor in ambient RNA.
    How to read: a value below the line means many reads come from empty droplets. Check the barcode rank plot and the ambient RNA before trusting the counts.
    Lines and annotations: the line is 0.7, the value 10x lists as expected for the fraction of reads in cells.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf
  column: value
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.7
  threshold_direction: min
  filter_expr: pl.col('metric') == 'fraction_reads_in_cells'
  caption: reads in cells against the 70% expectation

- component: card
  title: Valid barcodes
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average fraction of reads whose barcode matches the whitelist, shown against the expected minimum. It answers whether the barcode reads are of good quality.
    How to read: a value below the line points to a sequencing or chemistry problem with the barcode read. Look at the Q30 of the barcode in the summary table.
    Lines and annotations: the line is 0.75, the value 10x lists as expected for valid barcodes.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf
  column: value
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 0.75
  threshold_direction: min
  filter_expr: pl.col('metric') == 'valid_barcodes'
  caption: valid barcodes against the 75% expectation

- component: table
  title: Library metrics against expectations
  description: |-
    Each row is one metric of one sample with its value, the expected limit and a pass, warn or fail status. It answers which sample falls short on which metric.
    How to read: filter on status to list the metrics below their limit.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf

- component: figure
  id: mapping_stacked_bar
  title: Where reads map
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sample and its segments are the fraction of reads that map to exons, introns, intergenic regions or the antisense strand. It answers where the reads land.
    How to read: a high exonic share is typical of poly-A single-cell libraries. A large intronic share points to nuclei or nascent RNA, and a high antisense or intergenic share to a mapping or reference problem.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: fraction
    color: region
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      fraction: Fraction of reads
      region: Genomic region

- component: table
  title: Read mapping fractions
  description: |-
    Each row is the fraction of a sample's reads in one genomic region. It answers the exact values behind the bars.
    How to read: compare the same region across samples.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: marker_dotplot
  title: Marker genes per cluster
  description: |-
    Each dot is a gene in a cluster: its size is the share of cells expressing it and its colour the mean expression. It answers which genes mark which cluster.
    How to read: a large, dark dot in one cluster and small, pale dots elsewhere is a clean marker. A gene with big dots in many clusters is broadly expressed and does not identify a cell type.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: cluster_label
    gene: gene
    mean_expression: mean_expression
    frac_expressing: frac_expressing

- component: card
  title: Strongest marker expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest mean expression of any marker in any cluster, and the bars rank the clusters with the strongest marker. It answers which clusters carry the most strongly expressed markers.
    How to read: a cluster with a low top value has only weak markers, so its identity is harder to call.
  column: mean_expression
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: cluster_label
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: highest mean expression, by cluster

- component: card
  title: Mean marker expression
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median mean expression over the marker and cluster pairs, and the box shows its spread. It answers how strongly the markers are expressed overall.
    How to read: a median near zero means most pairs are off, as expected when each marker is specific to a cluster. A long upper tail holds the true markers.
  column: mean_expression
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: mean expression, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Share of cells expressing
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average share of cells that express a marker within a cluster, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how widely the markers are detected.
    How to read: markers expressed in most cells of a cluster are reliable. A pile at low shares shows markers seen in only a few cells.
  column: frac_expressing
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: share of cells expressing, over genes

- component: table
  title: Marker expression per cluster
  description: |-
    Each row is a marker gene in a cluster with its mean expression and the share of cells expressing it. It answers the exact values behind the dot plot.
    How to read: sort by the share of cells to find the most widely detected markers.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: marker_heatmap
  title: Marker expression across clusters
  description: |-
    Each row is a marker gene and each column a cluster, coloured by the mean expression of the gene in that cluster. It answers which clusters express which markers and which clusters resemble each other.
    How to read: a row that is bright in one column is a specific marker. Columns that cluster together share markers and may be related cell types or one over-split type.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn. Each row is scaled to a z-score over the clusters, so colours compare clusters for one gene and not genes with each other.
  kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    normalize: row_z
  roles:
    index: gene

- component: table
  title: Marker expression matrix
  description: |-
    Each row is a marker gene with its mean expression in every cluster. It answers the exact values behind the heatmap.
    How to read: read across a row to find the clusters that express the gene most.

- component: card
  title: Estimated cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the cells Cell Ranger estimates per sample, and the histogram shows the distribution. It answers how many cells each library yields.
    How to read: a sample far below the others may be under-loaded or have failed cell calling. Check its barcode rank plot.
  column: estimated_cells
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: estimated cells per sample

- component: card
  title: Genes per cell
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the per-sample median genes detected per cell, and the box shows its spread. It answers how complex the cells are.
    How to read: the value depends on cell type and depth, so compare samples of one experiment. A sample far below the rest is shallower or lower quality.
  column: median_genes_per_cell
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  - min
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median genes per cell, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Sequencing saturation
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average sequencing saturation, shown out of 100 percent. It answers how much more sequencing would reveal new UMIs.
    How to read: a high value means extra reads mostly repeat molecules already seen, so deeper sequencing gains little. A low value means the library is not yet saturated.
    Note: 10x gives no expected value for saturation, since it depends on sequencing depth and sample complexity, so no pass mark is drawn.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf
  column: sequencing_saturation_pct
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: saturation, of 100%

- component: card
  title: Reads in cells
  description: |-
    The hero number is the average percent of reads that fall in called cells, shown against the expected minimum. It answers how much of the sequencing goes to real cells.
    How to read: a value below the line means many reads come from empty droplets or ambient RNA. Check the barcode rank plot of that sample.
    Lines and annotations: the line is 70 percent, the value 10x lists as expected for the fraction of reads in cells.
    Source: https://assets.ctfassets.net/an68im79xiti/163qWiQBTVi2YLbskJphQX/e90bb82151b1cdab6d7e9b6c845e6130/CG000329_TechnicalNote_InterpretingCellRangerWebSummaryFiles_RevA.pdf
  column: fraction_reads_in_cells_pct
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - min
  secondary_layout: threshold
  threshold_value: 70.0
  threshold_direction: min
  caption: reads in cells against the 70% expectation

- component: table
  title: Cell Ranger metrics per sample
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample with its Cell Ranger metrics: cells, reads, saturation, Q30 values, mapping and detection counts. It answers the exact web summary numbers of a run.
    How to read: compare a column across samples to spot an outlier.

- component: figure
  id: pca_scree
  title: Variance explained per component
  description: |-
    Each bar is a principal component and its height is the fraction of the variance in the selected genes it explains. It answers how many components carry real signal.
    How to read: a steep drop followed by a flat tail marks the number of useful components. A flat profile with no elbow means little structure beyond noise, so check the clustering.
    Lines and annotations: no cut-off is drawn, since the number of components to keep is a choice made by reading the elbow.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: pc
    y: variance_explained
    color: sample
    labels:
      pc: Principal component
      variance_explained: Variance explained
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  title: Largest component variance
  description: |-
    The hero number is the variance explained by the strongest component, and the histogram shows the distribution over components. It answers how dominant the main axis of variation is.
    How to read: a first component far above the median means one strong axis, often cell type. Many similar small values mean variance spread thinly over components.
  column: variance_explained
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: variance explained, over components

- component: table
  title: PCA variance table
  description: |-
    Each row is a principal component with the fraction of variance it explains. It answers the exact values behind the scree bars.
    How to read: add the first rows to see the variance covered by the leading components.
